rules.statement: A gift inter vivos of property vesting in the donee with a prohibition against alienation, which is accepted by the donee, creates a fidei commissum that can be imposed by such act or last will.
rules.supporting_quote: "It would seem that Voet 36, 1, 9, would appear to consider that acceptance is as much required from the fidei commissarius as from the fiduciary donee. If the fidei commissarii did not accept the part of the gift designated for them before the death of the fiduciarius, the gift to her would be ultimate, and the plena proprietas would vest in the heirs of the fiduciarius on her death, and no acceptance thereafter could be of any avail."
